item.title: ⚡️ On October 30, the UN Security Council failed to extend the mandate of the UN Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara
item.description: ⚡️ On October 30, the UN Security Council failed to extend the mandate of the UN Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara ( #MINURSO ). ❌ The Russian delegation was compelled to vote against the relevant draft resolution prepared by the US. China, Pakistan and Somalia abstained . Apparently, the authors assumed that we would not block the extension of a UN operation headed by a Russian national and included provisions unacceptable to us and several other UN Security Council members . These provisions sought to enshrine a single option for resolving the Western Sahara issue, denying the people of Western Sahara the right to choose their own future and that of the land they have inhabited since the end of Spanish colonial rule in North Africa . 👉 Such an outcome would run counter to the principles and purposes of the UN Charter , including the principle of self-determination . ⚡️
On October 30, the UN Security Council
failed to extend the mandate
of
the UN Mission for the Referendum in Western Sahara
(
#MINURSO
).
❌
The Russian delegation was compelled
to vote
against
the relevant draft resolution prepared by the US.
China, Pakistan and Somalia
abstained
.
Apparently, the authors assumed that we would not block the extension of a UN operation headed by a Russian national and included
provisions unacceptable to us and several other UN Security Council members
.
These provisions sought to enshrine a single option for resolving the Western Sahara issue, denying the people of Western Sahara
the right to choose their own future
and that of
the land they have inhabited since the end of Spanish colonial rule in North Africa
.
👉
Such an outcome would run counter to the principles and purposes of
the UN Charter
, including
the principle of self-determination
.
The Russian Federation does not support
solutions imposed from outside through ultimatums. Any plans for a Western Sahara settlement must be developed
through negotiations
aimed at reaching
mutually acceptable agreements
, based on the relevant UN Security Council resolutions.
We are
disappointed
that US diplomats failed to distinguish between their own national position recognising Western Sahara as part of Morocco and their role as the informal lead on the Western Sahara file in the UN Security Council, which
requires them to act as an “honest broker”
.
Recognising the importance of MINURSO’s work, we submitted
an alternative short draft resolution
to the Security Council that
would have extended the Mission’s mandate for one year without any changes
, including to the parameters of the Western Sahara settlement. Unfortunately, only China and Somalia supported our draft.
The US voted against it
, while the remaining members abstained.
☝️
As a result, our proposal was not adopted.
We believe that
full responsibility
for winding down the UN presence in Western Sahara, which has long had a stabilising effect on the situation in the region,
lies with the US and the countries that sided with it.

item.title: 🇷🇺 Russia supplied nearly 14 million tonnes of food to Africa in the first nine months of 2026
item.description: 🇷🇺 🌍 Russia supplied nearly 14 million tonnes of food to Africa in the first nine months of 2026 From January to September 2026, Russia exported 13.9 million tonnes of food products to African countries, worth US$3.7 billion , according to the Federal Centre for the Development of Agricultural Product Exports (Agroexport). 📈 Compared with the same period in 2025, exports increased by 6% in volume and 9% in value . Africa accounted for 23% of Russia's total agricultural exports during this period. Egypt, Sudan, Kenya, Nigeria and Morocco were the continent's largest importers of Russian agricultural products. While grain remains the backbone of Russia's agricultural exports to Africa, there is considerable potential to expand supplies of other products and agricultural technologies , including seeds, vaccines, fertilisers and crop protection products. The Third Russia-Africa Summit , held in Moscow on 28-29 October , provided an important platform for advancing cooperation in agriculture, agricultural technology and professional training. ✍️ Among the agreements signed on the sidelines was a trilateral Memorandum of Understanding between Agroexport, the Timiryazev Russian State Agrarian University and the Tanzania Private Sector Federation, aimed at aligning Russian educational expertise with the needs of Tanzania's agricultural sector. 🤝 Russia remains committed to strengthening food security and expanding mutually beneficial agricultural cooperation with African countries. #

Russia supplied nearly 14 million tonnes of food to Africa in the first nine months of 2026
From January to September 2026, Russia exported 13.9 million tonnes of food products to African countries, worth
US$3.7 billion
, according to the Federal Centre for the Development of Agricultural Product Exports (Agroexport).
📈
Compared with the same period in 2025, exports increased by
6% in volume and 9% in value
.
Africa accounted for
23% of Russia's total agricultural exports
during this period. Egypt, Sudan, Kenya, Nigeria and Morocco were the continent's largest importers of Russian agricultural products.
While grain remains the backbone of Russia's agricultural exports to Africa, there is considerable potential to
expand supplies of other products and agricultural technologies
, including seeds, vaccines, fertilisers and crop protection products.
The
Third Russia-Africa Summit
, held in Moscow on 28-29 October
, provided an important platform for advancing cooperation in agriculture, agricultural technology and professional training.
✍️
Among the agreements signed on the sidelines was a
trilateral Memorandum of Understanding
between Agroexport, the Timiryazev Russian State Agrarian University and the Tanzania Private Sector Federation, aimed at aligning Russian educational expertise with the needs of Tanzania's agricultural sector.
🤝
Russia remains committed to
strengthening food security and expanding mutually beneficial agricultural cooperation with African countries.
#RussiaAfrica
#RussiaWithAfrica

item.title: 🎙 Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova's statement on Latvia’s presidency of the UN Security Council
item.description: 🎙 Russian Foreign Ministry Spokeswoman Maria Zakharova's statement on Latvia’s presidency of the UN Security Council (November 3, 2026) 💬 On November 1, Latvia assumed the presidency of the UN Security Council for one month , in accordance with the rotation principle . At the same time, we harbour no illusions about Riga’s intention to follow the impartial approaches outlined above. item.title: 🇷🇺 On November 1, Russia's Federation Council delegation led by its Speaker Valentina Matvienko
item.description: 🇷🇺 🇨🇳 On November 1, Russia's Federation Council delegation led by its Speaker Valentina Matvienko arrived in the People’s Republic of China. On November 2, Valentina Matvienko and Chairman of the Standing Committee of China’s National People’s Congress Zhao Leji held a meeting in Beijing . During their talks at the Great Hall of the People, the two officials noted that regular and productive interparliamentary ties reflect t he high level of Russia-China cooperation . They emphasised that President of Russia Vladimir Putin and President of China Xi Jinping maintain close contact ( 1 , 2 , 3 ). At their meetings in Beijing and Bishkek this year, the Leaders reached important agreements that set the course for cooperation between Russia and China. Their next meeting is scheduled to take place on the sidelines of the Summit in Shenzhen . Valentina Matvienko briefed her Chinese counterpart on the results of Russia’s recent parliamentary elections .
